questions.text_english: Identify the correct statement :

options.A: अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता एक प्रायोगिक मात्रा है।
options.B: जटिल अभिक्रियाओं के लिए आण्विकता का कोई अर्थ नहीं होता।
options.C: अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता शून्य अथवा भिन्नात्मक भी हो सकती है।
options.D: रासायनिक अभिक्रियाओं में तीन से अधिक आण्विकता अत्यधिक आम है।

options_english.A: Molecularity of a reaction is an experimental quantity.
options_english.B: For complex reactions molecularity has no meaning.
options_english.C: Molecularity of a reaction can be zero or even a fraction.
options_english.D: Molecularity more than three is very common in chemical reactions.

questions.solution: Option (B) is correct because molecularity is defined only for elementary (single-step) reactions and has no meaning for complex (multi-step) reactions, where only the rate-determining step has a defined molecularity. Option (A) is wrong because molecularity is a theoretical concept, not an experimental one — order is experimentally determined. Option (C) is wrong because molecularity is always a positive integer (1, 2, or 3) and can never be zero or a fraction. Option (D) is wrong because molecularity greater than three is extremely rare, not common, since the probability of simultaneous collision of more than three molecules is negligibly small.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया पर विचार कीजिए : Zn(s) + Ag₂O(s) + H₂O(l) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s) + 2OH⁻(aq)
दिया है : E°Ag⁺/Ag = 0.80 V, E°Zn²⁺/Zn = −0.76 V, 1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹
उपरोक्त अभिक्रिया की ΔᵣG° है :
questions.text_english:
Consider the following reaction : Zn(s) + Ag₂O(s) + H₂O(l) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s) + 2OH⁻(aq)
Given : E°Ag⁺/Ag = 0.80 V, E°Zn²⁺/Zn = −0.76 V, 1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹
ΔᵣG° for the above reaction is :
questions.solution: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.80 − (−0.76) = 1.56 V. The number of electrons transferred (n) = 2. ΔᵣG° = −nFE°cell = −2 × 96500 × 1.56 = −301,080 J mol⁻¹ = −301.080 kJ mol⁻¹. Therefore option (A) is correct. Option (C) and (D) arise from incorrect n values, and option (B) has the wrong sign indicating a non-spontaneous reaction, which contradicts the positive E°cell.

questions.text: क्रोमियम का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास है
questions.text_english: Electronic configuration of chromium is :
questions.solution: Chromium (Z = 24) has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹, making option (C) correct. The expected configuration based on the Aufbau principle would be [Ar] 3d⁴ 4s², but chromium attains extra stability by having a half-filled 3d subshell (3d⁵), so one electron from 4s shifts to 3d. Options (A), (B), and (D) are incorrect as they do not represent the actual stable configuration of chromium.

questions.text:
दी हुई अभिक्रिया की कोटि है
A + 2B → उत्पादों
वेग = k[A]^(1/2) [B]¹
questions.text_english:
The order for the given reaction is :
A + 2B → Products
Rate = k[A]^(1/2) [B]¹
questions.solution: The overall order of a reaction is the sum of the powers (exponents) of the concentration terms in the rate law. Here, Rate = k[A]^(1/2)[B]¹, so the order with respect to A is 1/2 = 0.5, and the order with respect to B is 1. The overall order = 0.5 + 1 = 1.5. Therefore option (A) is correct. Options (B), (C), and (D) result from adding only one exponent or using incorrect values.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन हेटरोलेप्टिक संकुल है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is heteroleptic complex ?
questions.solution: A heteroleptic complex is one that contains two or more different types of ligands. In [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺, the central metal cobalt is bonded to both NH₃ and Cl⁻ ligands, making it heteroleptic — option (D) is correct. Options (A), (B), and (C) are homoleptic complexes because each contains only one type of ligand (NH₃ or H₂O respectively).

questions.text: संकुल [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] का सही IUPAC नाम है
questions.text_english: The correct IUPAC name of the complex [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] is :
questions.solution: In IUPAC nomenclature, ligands are listed alphabetically before the metal. NH₃ (ammine) comes before Cl⁻ (chlorido) alphabetically, so the name begins with diammine then dichlorido. The oxidation state of Pt: let it be x; x + 0×2 + (−1)×2 = 0, so x = +2, giving platinum(II). The correct name is diamminedichloridoplatinum(II), which is option (B). Options (A) and (C) incorrectly assign oxidation state IV, and option (D) places chlorido before ammine.

questions.text: दिए हुए यौगिकों के क्वथनांकों के सही बढ़ते क्रम को पहचानिए :
questions.text_english: Identify the correct increasing order of boiling points of the given compounds :
questions.solution: Boiling points of alcohols increase with molecular mass. Among isomers, branching lowers the boiling point because it reduces the surface area available for van der Waals interactions. Propan-1-ol (3C, bp ~97°C) < butan-2-ol (4C, branched, bp ~99°C) < butan-1-ol (4C, straight chain, bp ~117°C) < pentan-1-ol (5C, bp ~138°C). This matches option (C). Options (A) and (B) place butan-2-ol above butan-1-ol incorrectly or reverse the overall order.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अणुओं में से किसकी प्रकृति काइरल है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following molecules is chiral in nature ?
questions.solution: A molecule is chiral if it has a carbon atom bearing four different groups (a chiral centre). Butan-2-ol (CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃) has C-2 bearing OH, H, CH₃, and C₂H₅ — four different groups — making it chiral, so option (B) is correct. Propan-2-ol has C-2 bearing OH, H, and two CH₃ groups, so it is achiral. 1-Bromobutane has no chiral centre. 2-Bromopropane (CH₃CHBrCH₃) has two identical CH₃ groups on the central carbon, so it is also achiral.

questions.text: क्षारक जो DNA में उपस्थित है, लेकिन RNA में नहीं है
questions.text_english: The base which is present in DNA but not in RNA is :
questions.solution: Thymine is a pyrimidine base found exclusively in DNA. In RNA, thymine is replaced by Uracil. Both DNA and RNA contain Adenine, Guanine, and Cytosine. Therefore option (C) is correct. Options (A), (B), and (D) are incorrect because Guanine, Cytosine, and Adenine are present in both DNA and RNA.

questions.text: लीथियम एल्युमिनियम हाइड्राइड के साथ एथेननाइट्राइल के अपचयन द्वारा उत्पादित यौगिक को पहचानिए :
questions.text_english: Identify the compound produced by the reduction of Ethanenitrile with Lithium aluminium hydride :
questions.solution: Ethanenitrile is CH₃CN (acetonitrile, 2 carbons). When reduced with LiAlH₄, the C≡N triple bond is converted to a C–N single bond, giving a primary amine. The product is CH₃CH₂NH₂, which is ethylamine. The number of carbon atoms is preserved (2 carbons), so the product is ethylamine, not methylamine (1C) or propylamine (3C). Option (A) is correct. Option (B), ethanal, would result from reduction of an ester or acid chloride, not a nitrile.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं में से किसका स्पष्टीकरण ग्लूकोस की विवृत शृंखला संरचना द्वारा नहीं किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following reactions is not explained by the open chain structure of glucose ?

options.A: Glucose on prolonged heating with HI forms n-hexane.
options.B: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.
options.C: Glucose gets oxidized to gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water.
options.D: Glucose exists in two different crystalline forms, alpha (α) and beta (β).

options_english.A: Glucose on prolonged heating with HI forms n-hexane.
options_english.B: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.
options_english.C: Glucose gets oxidized to gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water.
options_english.D: Glucose exists in two different crystalline forms, alpha (α) and beta (β).

questions.solution: The existence of glucose in two crystalline forms — α-D-glucose and β-D-glucose — is explained by the cyclic (ring) structure of glucose, specifically by the formation of a hemiacetal ring and the creation of a new chiral centre at C-1 (anomeric carbon). This phenomenon, called mutarotation, cannot be explained by the open-chain structure. Options (A), (B), and (C) are all explained by the open-chain structure, which contains an aldehyde group. Therefore option (D) is correct.

questions.text: प्रोटीन α-ऐमीनो अम्लों के बहुलक होते हैं जो आपस में जुड़े होते हैं
questions.text_english: Proteins are polymers of α-amino acids which are joined to each other by :
questions.solution: Proteins are formed by the polymerization of α-amino acids through peptide bonds. A peptide bond (–CO–NH–) is formed when the carboxyl group of one amino acid reacts with the amino group of another amino acid with the elimination of water. Option (B) is therefore correct. A glycosidic bond links monosaccharides in carbohydrates (option C is wrong). A coordinate bond is found in coordination compounds (D is wrong). While a peptide bond is technically a type of covalent bond, option (A) is too vague and (B) is the specific and correct answer.

कारण (R) : इन तत्वों की मूल अवस्थाओं तथा सामान्य ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं में इनके कक्षक पूर्ण भरित होते हैं।

Assertion (A) : Zinc, cadmium and mercury are not considered as transition elements.
Reason (R) : These elements have completely filled orbitals in their ground state as well as in their common oxidation states.
questions.instruction_line: दोनों कथनों को पढ़कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Read both statements and select the correct answer.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. Transition elements are defined as those that have an incompletely filled d subshell in the elemental form or in any of their common oxidation states. Zinc (Zn), Cadmium (Cd), and Mercury (Hg) have completely filled d¹⁰ subshells in both their ground states and their most common oxidation states (Zn²⁺ has 3d¹⁰). Since their d subshells are always filled, they do not qualify as transition elements. The reason thus directly and correctly explains the assertion, making option (A) correct.

2HI → H₂ + I₂
कारण (R) : अभिकारकों के दो अणुओं का आपस में एक साथ संघट्ट होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The molecularity of the given reaction is 2
2HI → H₂ + I₂
Reason (R) : Two molecules of the reactants are involved in simultaneous collision between them.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The decomposition of HI (2HI → H₂ + I₂) is a bimolecular reaction. Two HI molecules collide simultaneously to break and form bonds, giving a molecularity of 2. The assertion is correct because the stoichiometry of this elementary reaction corresponds directly to the molecularity. The reason is also correct and explains the assertion accurately: the molecularity equals 2 precisely because two reactant molecules participate in a simultaneous collision. Therefore option (A) is correct.

Assertion (A) : Glucose gets oxidized to six carbon gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water.
Reason (R) : The carbonyl group is absent in the open chain structure of glucose.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: glucose reacts with bromine water (a mild oxidizing agent) to give gluconic acid, a 6-carbon carboxylic acid, confirming the presence of an aldehyde group in glucose. However, the Reason is false: the open-chain structure of glucose does contain a carbonyl group — specifically an aldehyde group (–CHO) at C-1. In fact, it is precisely because of this aldehyde group that glucose is oxidized by bromine water. Therefore option (C) is correct: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

Assertion (A) : Aromatic primary amines can be prepared by Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis.
Reason (R) : Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The Assertion is false: Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis cannot be used to prepare aromatic primary amines. It is used only for aliphatic primary amines. The synthesis requires aryl halides to undergo nucleophilic substitution, but aryl halides are resistant to nucleophilic substitution due to resonance delocalization of the lone pair of the halogen into the ring. The Reason is true: aryl halides indeed do not undergo nucleophilic substitution reactions with the phthalimide anion, which is precisely why the synthesis fails for aromatic amines. Therefore option (D) is correct — the Assertion is false but the Reason is true.

sub_questions.text: उपसहसंयोजन संख्या की परिभाषा लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Define coordination number.

key_points: The coordination number of a metal ion in a complex is the total number of donor atoms (ligand atoms) directly bonded to the central metal ion.

sub_questions.solution: The coordination number of a central metal ion in a coordination compound is the total number of ligand donor atoms that are directly bonded to the metal ion. For example, in [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, cobalt has a coordination number of 6, since six nitrogen atoms from six NH₃ ligands are directly bonded to it.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित संकुल द्वारा प्रदर्शित समावयवता का प्रकार इंगित कीजिए : [Co(en)₃]Cl₃
sub_questions.text_english: Indicate the type of isomerism exhibited by the following complex : [Co(en)₃]Cl₃

key_points: Optical isomerism (specifically enantiomerism)

sub_questions.solution: [Co(en)₃]Cl₃ exhibits optical isomerism. The complex has three bidentate ethylenediamine (en) ligands coordinated to Co³⁺, giving it a tris-chelate octahedral geometry with no plane of symmetry. This results in two non-superimposable mirror images (d and l forms), making the complex optically active.

(a) Why second ionization enthalpies of chromium and copper are exceptionally higher than those of their neighbouring elements ?

sub_questions.text: क्रोमियम और कॉपर की द्वितीय आयनन एन्थैल्पी अपने समीपवर्ती तत्वों की द्वितीय आयनन एन्थैल्पी की अपेक्षा असाधारण रूप से उच्चतर क्यों होती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why second ionization enthalpies of chromium and copper are exceptionally higher than those of their neighbouring elements ?

key_points: Cr and Cu have configurations [Ar]3d⁵4s¹ and [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ respectively. After losing the first electron (from 4s), Cr⁺ has [Ar]3d⁵ (half-filled) and Cu⁺ has [Ar]3d¹⁰ (fully filled), which are extra stable configurations. Removing the second electron disturbs this stability, requiring exceptionally high energy.

sub_questions.solution: Chromium has the configuration [Ar]3d⁵4s¹ and copper has [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹. After removing the first electron (from 4s), Cr⁺ acquires the stable half-filled 3d⁵ configuration and Cu⁺ acquires the stable fully-filled 3d¹⁰ configuration. Since these configurations are especially stable, removing the second electron from them requires an exceptionally large amount of energy, hence the second ionization enthalpy is abnormally high compared to neighbouring elements.

sub_questions.text: संक्रमण तत्व अंतराकाशी यौगिक क्यों बनाते हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why transition elements form interstitial compounds ?

key_points: Transition metals have large atomic sizes with interstitial voids in their crystal lattices. Small atoms like H, C, N can fit into these voids to form interstitial compounds.

sub_questions.solution: Transition elements have large atomic sizes and closely packed crystal structures with small interstitial voids or gaps. Small non-metallic atoms such as hydrogen, carbon, boron, and nitrogen are small enough to fit into these interstitial voids without significantly distorting the metal lattice, resulting in the formation of interstitial compounds such as TiC, Fe₃C, and TiH₂.

questions.text:
(A) किसी प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया में अभिकारक की सांद्रता 5 मिनट में 0.6 mol L⁻¹ से घटकर 0.2 mol L⁻¹ रह जाती है। अभिक्रिया के लिए वेग स्थिरांक परिकलित कीजिए। (log 3 = 0.48)
अथवा
(B) किसी प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया के लिए वेग स्थिरांक, k, 2.54 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ है। अभिकारक के तीन-चौथाई विघटन के लिए लगने वाले समय की गणना कीजिए। (log 4 = 0.60)
questions.text_english:
(A) The concentration of the reactant is reduced from 0.6 mol L⁻¹ to 0.2 mol L⁻¹ in 5 minutes in a first order reaction. Calculate rate constant of the reaction. (log 3 = 0.48)
OR
(B) Rate constant k for the first order reaction is 2.54 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Calculate the time required for three-fourth of the reactant to decompose. (log 4 = 0.60)
questions.solution:
Option A: For a first order reaction, k = (2.303/t) × log([A]₀/[A]t). Here t = 5 min, [A]₀ = 0.6 mol L⁻¹, [A]t = 0.2 mol L⁻¹. So k = (2.303/5) × log(0.6/0.2) = (2.303/5) × log 3 = (0.4606) × 0.48 = 0.2211 min⁻¹.

Option B: For 3/4 decomposition, [A]t = [A]₀ − (3/4)[A]₀ = [A]₀/4. Therefore [A]₀/[A]t = 4. t = (2.303/k) × log 4 = (2.303/2.54 × 10⁻³) × 0.60 = 906.7 × 0.60 ≈ 544 s.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the major product in the following reaction : Chlorobenzene + CH₃–Cl → (Na / dry ether) → ?

key_points: Toluene (methylbenzene, C₆H₅CH₃)

sub_questions.solution: This is a Wurtz-Fittig reaction. When chlorobenzene (an aryl halide) reacts with methyl chloride (an alkyl halide) in the presence of sodium metal and dry ether, the two halides are coupled to form toluene (C₆H₅CH₃). The sodium removes the halogen atoms and links the aryl and alkyl groups together.

sub_questions.text: क्या होता है जब 2-ब्रोमो-ब्यूटेन की ऐल्कोहॉली पोटैशियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड के साथ अभिक्रिया कराई जाती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What happens when 2-Bromobutane is made to react with alcoholic potassium hydroxide ?

key_points: Elimination (E2) reaction occurs. Alcoholic KOH acts as a base and abstracts a β-hydrogen, leading to dehydrobromination to give but-2-ene (major product, by Saytzeff's rule) and but-1-ene (minor product).

sub_questions.solution: When 2-bromobutane reacts with alcoholic KOH, an elimination reaction (dehydrohalogenation) occurs. Alcoholic KOH acts as a base and removes a β-hydrogen from the adjacent carbon while the bromide ion leaves, forming an alkene. According to Saytzeff's rule, the major product is but-2-ene (the more substituted alkene) and the minor product is but-1-ene.

questions.text:
60 g ग्लूकोस को 250 g जल में घोला जाता है। इस विलयन का हिमांक परिकलित कीजिए।
(ग्लूकोस का मोलर द्रव्यमान = 180 g mol⁻¹, जल के लिए Kf = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)
questions.text_english:
60 g of glucose is dissolved in 250 g of water. Calculate the freezing point of this solution.
(molar mass of glucose = 180 g mol⁻¹, Kf for water = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)

key_points: Moles of glucose = 60/180 = 1/3 mol
Mass of solvent = 250 g = 0.250 kg
Molality (m) = (1/3)/0.250 = 4/3 mol kg⁻¹
Freezing point = 0 − 2.48 = −2.48°C

questions.solution: Step 1: Moles of glucose = mass/molar mass = 60/180 = 1/3 mol. Step 2: Mass of solvent (water) = 250 g = 0.250 kg. Step 3: Molality (m) = moles of solute/mass of solvent in kg = (1/3)/0.250 = 4/3 = 1.333 mol kg⁻¹. Step 4: Depression in freezing point, ΔTf = Kf × m = 1.86 × 1.333 = 2.48 K. Step 5: Freezing point of solution = Freezing point of pure water − ΔTf = 0°C − 2.48°C = −2.48°C. The freezing point of the solution is −2.48°C.

questions.text:
298 K पर निम्नलिखित सेल का emf परिकलित कीजिए :
Sn | Sn²⁺ (0.001 M) || H⁺ (0.01 M) | H₂(g) (1 bar) | Pt(s)
दिया है : E°Sn²⁺/Sn = −0.14 V, E°H⁺/H₂ = 0.00 V [log 10 = 1]
questions.text_english:
Calculate emf of the following cell at 298 K :
Sn | Sn²⁺ (0.001 M) || H⁺ (0.01 M) | H₂(g) (1 bar) | Pt(s)
Given : E°Sn²⁺/Sn = −0.14 V, E°H⁺/H₂ = 0.00 V [log 10 = 1]

key_points: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.00 − (−0.14) = 0.14 V
Cell reaction: Sn + 2H⁺ → Sn²⁺ + H₂, n = 2
Nernst equation: Ecell = 0.14 − (0.0591/2) × log([Sn²⁺]/[H⁺]²)

questions.solution: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.00 − (−0.14) = +0.14 V. The cell reaction is: Sn(s) + 2H⁺(aq) → Sn²⁺(aq) + H₂(g), where n = 2. Applying the Nernst equation at 298 K: Ecell = E°cell − (0.0591/n) × log([Sn²⁺]/[H⁺]²). Substituting values: Ecell = 0.14 − (0.0591/2) × log(0.001/(0.01)²) = 0.14 − 0.02955 × log(0.001/0.0001) = 0.14 − 0.02955 × log(10) = 0.14 − 0.02955 × 1 = 0.14 − 0.02955 ≈ 0.1105 V. The emf of the cell at 298 K is approximately 0.11 V.

sub_questions.text_english:

key_points: (i) 2Na₂CrO₄ + 2H⁺ → Na₂Cr₂O₇ + 2Na⁺ + H₂O (or: 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ → Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O)

sub_questions.text: लैंथेनॉयडों की अपेक्षा ऐक्टिनॉयडों का रसायन जटिल क्यों होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is chemistry of actinoids complicated as compared to lanthanoids ?

key_points: Actinoids show a much wider range of oxidation states (+3 to +7) compared to lanthanoids (mainly +3)
5f orbitals of actinoids are less deeply buried and participate in bonding
Many actinoids are radioactive, complicating their study

sub_questions.solution: The chemistry of actinoids is more complex than that of lanthanoids for three main reasons. First, actinoids exhibit a much wider range of oxidation states (from +3 to +7) because the 5f, 6d, and 7s orbitals are close in energy and all can participate in bonding. In contrast, lanthanoids show predominantly the +3 oxidation state. Second, the 5f orbitals of actinoids are less shielded and closer in energy to the outer orbitals, allowing greater participation in bonding and complex formation. Third, most actinoids are radioactive, making their experimental study more difficult.

questions.text:
(a) समझाइए कि [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺ प्रबल अनुचुंबकीय है जबकि [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ दुर्बल अनुचुंबकीय है। [Fe का परमाणु क्रमांक = 26]
(b) क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत के आधार पर, d⁵ आयन का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास लिखिए जिसके लिए Δ₀ < P है।
questions.text_english:
(a) Explain why [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺ is strongly paramagnetic whereas [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ is weakly paramagnetic. [Atomic number of Fe = 26]
(b) On the basis of crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration for d⁵ ion for which Δ₀ < P.

sub_questions.text: समझाइए कि [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺ प्रबल अनुचुंबकीय है जबकि [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ दुर्बल अनुचुंबकीय है।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain why [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺ is strongly paramagnetic whereas [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ is weakly paramagnetic.

key_points: Fe³⁺ has 3d⁵ configuration (5 electrons in d orbitals)
H₂O is a weak field ligand → small Δ₀ → high spin → 5 unpaired electrons → strongly paramagnetic
CN⁻ is a strong field ligand → large Δ₀ → low spin → t₂g⁵ eg⁰ → 1 unpaired electron → weakly paramagnetic

sub_questions.solution: Iron in both complexes is Fe³⁺, which has the 3d⁵ configuration. H₂O is a weak field ligand, so it produces a small crystal field splitting energy (Δ₀). Since Δ₀ is less than the pairing energy (P), the electrons occupy the d orbitals according to Hund's rule, giving a high spin configuration: t₂g³ eg², with 5 unpaired electrons. This makes [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺ strongly paramagnetic. CN⁻ is a strong field ligand, producing a large Δ₀ that exceeds P. Electrons are forced to pair up in the lower t₂g orbitals, giving a low spin configuration: t₂g⁵ eg⁰, with only 1 unpaired electron. Hence [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ is weakly paramagnetic.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत के आधार पर, d⁵ आयन का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास लिखिए जिसके लिए Δ₀ < P है।
sub_questions.text_english: On the basis of crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration for d⁵ ion for which Δ₀ < P.

key_points: t₂g³ eg² (high spin configuration, 5 unpaired electrons)

sub_questions.solution: When Δ₀ < P (crystal field splitting is less than pairing energy), the complex is high spin. For a d⁵ ion in an octahedral field with Δ₀ < P, electrons occupy all five d orbitals singly before pairing. The electronic configuration is t₂g³ eg², with 5 unpaired electrons.

(a) Write the IUPAC name of the given compound : CH₃CH(CH₃)CH(Br)CH₃
(b) Define Racemisation.
(c) The boiling points of the alkyl halides with the same alkyl group decrease in the given order : RI > RBr > RCl > RF. Explain the above statement.

sub_questions.text: दिए गए यौगिक को IUPAC नाम लिखिए : CH₃CH(CH₃)CH(Br)CH₃
sub_questions.text_english: Write the IUPAC name of the given compound : CH₃CH(CH₃)CH(Br)CH₃

key_points: 2-bromo-3-methylbutane

sub_questions.solution: The compound CH₃CH(CH₃)CH(Br)CH₃ has the parent chain of 4 carbons (butane). There is a bromo group on C-2 and a methyl group on C-3 (numbering from the end closer to the bromo group). The IUPAC name is 2-bromo-3-methylbutane.

sub_questions.text: रेसिमीकरण को परिभाषित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Define Racemisation.

key_points: Racemisation is the process by which an optically active compound (pure enantiomer) is converted into a racemic mixture (equal amounts of d and l forms) that has no net optical rotation.

sub_questions.solution: Racemisation is the process in which a pure enantiomer (optically active compound) is converted into a racemic mixture, which contains equal amounts of the d (dextrorotatory) and l (laevorotatory) forms. A racemic mixture shows no net optical rotation because the optical rotations of the two enantiomers cancel each other out.

sub_questions.text: समान ऐल्किल समूह के लिए ऐल्किल हैलाइडों के क्वथनांकों के घटने का क्रम : RI > RBr > RCl > RF है। उपरोक्त कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: The boiling points of the alkyl halides with the same alkyl group decrease in the given order : RI > RBr > RCl > RF. Explain the above statement.

key_points: Boiling point depends on the magnitude of van der Waals (London dispersion) forces. Larger, more polarisable atoms lead to stronger dispersion forces and higher boiling points. Iodine is the most polarisable halogen, followed by Br, Cl, and F, hence RI has the highest boiling point.

sub_questions.solution: The boiling points of alkyl halides with the same alkyl group decrease in the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF because boiling point depends on the strength of van der Waals (London dispersion) forces between molecules. These forces increase with the size and polarisability of the halogen atom. Iodine is the largest and most polarisable halogen, so RI has the strongest intermolecular attractions and the highest boiling point. Fluorine is the smallest and least polarisable, so RF has the weakest attractions and the lowest boiling point.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में सम्मिलित अभिक्रियाएँ लिखिए :
(a) रोजेनमुंड अपचयन
(b) कैनिज़ारो अभिक्रिया
(c) हेल–फोलार्ड–जेलिंस्की अभिक्रिया
questions.text_english:
Write the reaction involved in
(a) Rosenmund's reduction
(b) Cannizzaro's reaction
(c) Hell – Volhard – Zelinsky reaction

sub_questions.text: रोजेनमुंड अपचयन
sub_questions.text_english: Rosenmund's reduction

key_points: Acid chloride (RCOCl) is reduced to aldehyde (RCHO) using H₂ gas over a palladium catalyst poisoned with BaSO₄. RCOCI + H₂ → RCHO + HCI

sub_questions.solution: Rosenmund's reduction involves the reduction of an acid chloride to an aldehyde using hydrogen gas (H₂) in the presence of a palladium catalyst supported on barium sulphate (Pd/BaSO₄, a poisoned catalyst): RCOCl + H₂ → RCHO + HCl. The catalyst is poisoned to prevent further reduction of the aldehyde to alcohol.

sub_questions.text: कैनिज़ारो अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Cannizzaro's reaction

key_points: Aldehydes without α-hydrogen undergo disproportionation with conc. KOH: one molecule is oxidised to carboxylate salt and another is reduced to alcohol. 2HCHO + KOH → HCOOK + CH₃OH

sub_questions.solution: Cannizzaro's reaction is a disproportionation reaction that occurs with aldehydes lacking α-hydrogen atoms. When treated with concentrated KOH, one molecule of aldehyde is oxidized to a carboxylate salt (or carboxylic acid) while another is reduced to an alcohol. For example: 2HCHO + KOH → HCOOK + CH₃OH (formaldehyde gives potassium formate and methanol).

sub_questions.text: हेल–फोलार्ड–जेलिंस्की अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Hell – Volhard – Zelinsky reaction

key_points: Carboxylic acids react with Cl₂ or Br₂ in the presence of red phosphorus (P) to give α-halogenated acid. CH₃COOH + Cl₂ (P) → ClCH₂COOH + HCl

sub_questions.solution: The Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction involves the halogenation of carboxylic acids at the α-carbon using Cl₂ or Br₂ in the presence of red phosphorus (P). For example, acetic acid with Cl₂ and P gives chloroacetic acid: CH₃COOH + Cl₂ → ClCH₂COOH + HCl. Red phosphorus converts a small amount of the acid to its acid halide, which undergoes enolisation and halogenation more readily.

questions.text_english:
(A) (a) Define the following terms :
(i) Invert Sugar
(ii) Polysaccharides
(b) On the basis of structure differentiate between fibrous and globular proteins.
OR
(B) (a) Why is glycogen known as animal starch ?
(b) Differentiate between essential amino acids and non-essential amino acids.
(c) What is the effect of denaturation on the structure of proteins ?

sub_questions.text: अपवृत्त शर्करा
sub_questions.text_english: Invert Sugar

key_points: Invert sugar is the equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose obtained by the hydrolysis (acid or enzyme) of sucrose. The rotation changes from +66.5° (dextrorotatory sucrose) to −19.8° (the mixture is laevorotatory).

sub_questions.solution: Invert sugar is the equimolar mixture of D-(+)-glucose and D-(−)-fructose produced by the hydrolysis of sucrose. Sucrose is dextrorotatory (+66.5°), but after hydrolysis, the product mixture is laevorotatory (−19.8°) because fructose's strong laevo-rotation dominates. The change in sign of optical rotation is termed inversion, hence the product is called invert sugar.

sub_questions.text: पॉलिसैकेराइड
sub_questions.text_english: Polysaccharides

key_points: Polysaccharides are carbohydrates consisting of long chains of monosaccharide units linked together by glycosidic bonds. Examples: starch, cellulose, glycogen.

sub_questions.solution: Polysaccharides are complex carbohydrates made up of large numbers of monosaccharide units joined to each other by glycosidic bonds. They serve as energy storage (starch, glycogen) or structural (cellulose, chitin) materials in living organisms. Examples include starch and cellulose (both made of glucose units), where starch is digestible and cellulose is not.

sub_questions.text: संरचना के आधार पर रेशेदार प्रोटीन और गोलिकाकार प्रोटीन में अंतर कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: On the basis of structure differentiate between fibrous and globular proteins.

key_points: Fibrous proteins: polypeptide chains are arranged in parallel and held together by hydrogen and disulphide bonds, forming long fibre-like structures. They are insoluble in water. Examples: keratin, myosin, collagen.
Globular proteins: polypeptide chains are coiled around themselves into a compact spherical shape. They are generally soluble in water. Examples: insulin, haemoglobin, enzymes.

sub_questions.solution: Fibrous proteins have polypeptide chains arranged in long parallel strands or sheets, held together by hydrogen bonds and disulphide bridges. They are tough, insoluble in water, and serve structural functions. Examples include keratin (hair, nails) and collagen (tendons). Globular proteins have polypeptide chains folded and coiled into compact, spherical shapes. They are generally soluble in water and perform dynamic functions such as catalysis (enzymes) and transport (haemoglobin). Examples include insulin and albumin.

sub_questions.text: ग्लाइकोज़न को प्राणी स्टार्च क्यों कहा जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is glycogen known as animal starch ?

key_points: Glycogen is the storage form of glucose in animals (stored in liver and muscle), just as starch is the storage polysaccharide in plants. Structurally, glycogen is highly branched, similar to amylopectin of starch.

sub_questions.solution: Glycogen is called animal starch because it serves the same function in animals (energy storage) as starch does in plants. It is a highly branched polysaccharide of glucose and is stored mainly in the liver and muscle cells. When energy is required, glycogen is hydrolysed to release glucose. Its structure is similar to amylopectin (a component of starch) but is more extensively branched.

sub_questions.text: आवश्यक और अनावश्यक ऐमीनो अम्लों में अंतर कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between essential amino acids and non-essential amino acids.

key_points: Essential amino acids cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be supplied through diet. Examples: valine, leucine, lysine.
Non-essential amino acids can be synthesized by the human body and need not be obtained from food. Examples: glycine, alanine, glutamic acid.

sub_questions.solution: Essential amino acids are those that the human body cannot synthesize on its own and must therefore be obtained from the diet. There are about 10 essential amino acids, including valine, leucine, lysine, and tryptophan. Non-essential amino acids, on the other hand, can be synthesized by the body from other metabolic intermediates and do not need to be supplied through food. Examples include glycine, alanine, and glutamic acid.

sub_questions.text: प्रोटीन की संरचना पर विकृतीकरण का क्या प्रभाव होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is the effect of denaturation on the structure of proteins ?

key_points: Denaturation disrupts the secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures of a protein by breaking hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, and disulphide bridges. The polypeptide chain unfolds and the protein loses its biological activity. The primary structure (amino acid sequence) remains intact.

sub_questions.solution: Denaturation disrupts the higher-order structures (secondary, tertiary, and quaternary) of a protein without breaking the peptide bonds in the primary structure. The hydrogen bonds, ionic interactions, and disulphide bridges that maintain the protein's 3D conformation are broken by heat, pH changes, or chemicals. As a result, the polypeptide chain unfolds and the protein loses its native shape and biological activity. Coagulation of egg white on boiling is a common example of denaturation.

questions.text_english: Osmosis is a process by which the molecules of a solvent pass from a solution of low solute concentration to a solution of high solute concentration through a semi-permeable membrane. Osmotic pressure is a colligative property. When the applied pressure on a solution exceeds its osmotic pressure, reverse osmosis occurs. When two solutions are separated by a semipermeable membrane and they have same osmotic pressure they are said to be isotonic. Of the two solutions separated by a semipermeable membrane, if one is a lower osmotic pressure, it is said to be hypotonic relative to the second solution. If it has a higher osmotic pressure, than the second solution, it is said to be hypertonic relative to the second solution. The osmotic pressure associated with the fluid inside the blood cell is equivalent to that of 0.9% (mass/volume) sodium chloride solution called normal saline solution and it is safe to inject intravenously. Osmotic pressure is vital in daily life and nature. It helps in explain, why IV fluids match blood's osmotic pressure, its also the principle behind food preservation using salt or sugar.

sub_questions.text_english:
Calculate the amount of CaCl₂ (i = 2.59) dissolved in 2.46 litre of water such that its osmotic pressure is 0.70 atm at 27°C.
[Given : R = 0.082 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, molar mass of CaCl₂ = 111 g mol⁻¹]

key_points: Moles of CaCl₂ = 0.01098 × 2.46 = 0.02701 mol

sub_questions.solution: Using the modified osmotic pressure equation for electrolytes: π = iCRT. Rearranging: C = π/(iRT) = 0.70/(2.59 × 0.082 × 300) = 0.70/63.762 = 0.01098 mol L⁻¹. Moles of CaCl₂ = C × V = 0.01098 × 2.46 = 0.02701 mol. Mass of CaCl₂ = moles × molar mass = 0.02701 × 111 ≈ 2.998 g ≈ 3.0 g. Therefore, approximately 3.0 g of CaCl₂ must be dissolved.

sub_questions.text_english: Why osmotic pressure is more advantageous than other colligative properties ?

key_points: Osmotic pressure can be measured at room temperature, the magnitude of osmotic pressure is large even for dilute solutions (making it measurable easily), and it is particularly useful for high molar mass substances like polymers and biomolecules.

sub_questions.solution: Osmotic pressure is more advantageous than other colligative properties because it can be measured at room temperature without heating or cooling. Even for very dilute solutions, the osmotic pressure is relatively large and easily measurable. This makes it especially suitable for determining the molar masses of macromolecules such as proteins, polymers, and colloids, where the other colligative effects (boiling point elevation, freezing point depression) are too small to measure accurately.

sub_questions.text_english: Which phenomenon is responsible for desalination of sea water ?

key_points: Reverse osmosis

sub_questions.solution: Reverse osmosis is responsible for the desalination of sea water. In this process, a pressure greater than the osmotic pressure of sea water is applied to it. This forces water molecules to pass from the region of high solute concentration (sea water) through a semi-permeable membrane to the region of low solute concentration (pure water), effectively removing dissolved salts.

questions.text_english: Like NH₃, nitrogen atom of amine is trivalent and carries an unshared pair of electrons. Nitrogen orbitals in amines are therefore sp³ hybridised and the geometry of amines is pyramidal. Lower aliphatic amines are soluble in water due to the formation of hydrogen bond with water molecules. The solubility decreases as the molar mass of amines increases due to increase in size of hydrophobic part. Higher amines are insoluble in water. However amines are less soluble in water than alcohols because of low electronegativity of nitrogen as compared to oxygen. Boiling points of isomeric amines follow the order 1° > 2° > 3°. It is due to the fact the amines are held together due to hydrogen bonding. Extent of hydrogen bonding is more in primary amines than in secondary amines as two hydrogen atoms are available for hydrogen bond formation. Tertiary amines do not show hydrogen bonding because of the absence of hydrogen atom attached to nitrogen. Amines can be prepared from, nitro compounds, nitriles, amides etc.

sub_questions.text_english: Why primary amines have higher boiling points than tertiary amines ?

key_points: Primary amines have two N–H bonds and can form extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Tertiary amines have no N–H bond and cannot form hydrogen bonds with each other, so they have lower boiling points.

sub_questions.solution: Primary amines have two hydrogen atoms bonded to the nitrogen atom, which allows them to form stronger and more extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other. These hydrogen bonds require more energy to break, resulting in higher boiling points. Tertiary amines, having no N–H bond, cannot engage in intermolecular hydrogen bonding with each other and hence have significantly lower boiling points despite higher molecular masses.

sub_questions.solution: Molar conductivity: Λm = (κ × 1000)/c = (1.06 × 10⁻² × 1000)/0.1 = 106 S cm² mol⁻¹. Limiting molar conductivity: Λ°m(NaCl) = λ°Na⁺ + λ°Cl⁻ = 50.1 + 76.5 = 126.6 S cm² mol⁻¹. Degree of dissociation: α = Λm/Λ°m = 106/126.6 = 0.837, i.e., 83.7%.

key_points: Current flows from the silver electrode (cathode/positive terminal) to the zinc electrode (anode/negative terminal) in the external circuit.

sub_questions.solution: In this galvanic cell, zinc is oxidized at the anode (negative electrode) and silver ions are reduced at the cathode (positive electrode). Electrons flow in the external circuit from the zinc anode (where oxidation occurs) to the silver cathode (where reduction occurs). Conventional current, however, flows in the opposite direction — from the cathode (silver/positive) to the anode (zinc/negative) in the external circuit.

sub_questions.text: प्राथमिक बैटरी और द्वितीयक बैटरी में अंतर कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between a primary battery and a secondary battery.

key_points: Primary battery: cannot be recharged, the electrode reactions are irreversible, used once until discharged. Example: dry cell.
Secondary battery: can be recharged by passing electric current, electrode reactions are reversible. Example: lead storage battery, lithium-ion battery.

sub_questions.solution: A primary battery is one in which the electrode reactions are irreversible. Once the chemicals are consumed, the battery cannot be recharged and must be discarded. An example is the Leclanché dry cell (Leclanche cell). A secondary battery is one in which the electrode reactions are reversible. After discharge, it can be recharged by passing an electric current in the reverse direction, restoring the original chemical composition. Examples include the lead storage battery (car battery) and the lithium-ion battery used in mobile phones.

key_points: Highly efficient (up to 70%) compared to conventional combustion engines.
Environmentally clean — the only by-product is water.
Continuous operation as long as fuel (H₂) and oxidant (O₂) are supplied.

sub_questions.solution: Two advantages of the H₂–O₂ fuel cell are: (i) it converts chemical energy directly into electrical energy with high efficiency (around 70%), far exceeding the efficiency of conventional combustion engines (about 40%); (ii) it is environmentally friendly because the only product of the reaction is water (H₂O), unlike fossil fuel combustion which produces CO₂ and other pollutants.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does the cell potential of mercury cell remain constant throughout the life ?

key_points: In a mercury cell, the overall reaction does not involve ions in solution. The electrolyte concentration does not change during discharge, so the cell potential remains constant throughout its life.

sub_questions.solution: The cell potential of a mercury cell remains constant throughout its life because the overall cell reaction does not involve any ion in solution. The anode reaction is Zn(Hg) + 2OH⁻ → ZnO(s) + H₂O + 2e⁻ and the cathode reaction is HgO(s) + H₂O + 2e⁻ → Hg(l) + 2OH⁻. Since no ionic concentration changes in the electrolyte during discharge, the cell EMF (determined by the Nernst equation) remains unchanged throughout the battery's life.

sub_questions.text_english: An organic compound 'A', with molecular formula C₂H₆O... Identify 'A', 'B', 'C', 'D' and 'E' and write all the reactions involved.

key_points: A = Ethanol (C₂H₅OH)
B = Sodium ethoxide (C₂H₅ONa)
C = Iodoform (CHI₃) — from iodoform test
D = Diethyl ether (C₂H₅OC₂H₅, C₄H₁₀O) — from intermolecular dehydration at 413K
E = Ethyl iodide (C₂H₅I) — from reaction of diethyl ether with excess HI

sub_questions.solution: A is ethanol (C₂H₅OH). Ethanol reacts with sodium to give sodium ethoxide (B = C₂H₅ONa) and H₂: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂. Ethanol with I₂ and NaOH gives iodoform (C = CHI₃) and sodium acetate: C₂H₅OH + 3I₂ + 3NaOH → CHI₃ + HCOONa + 3NaI + 3H₂O. Ethanol at 413 K with H₂SO₄ undergoes intermolecular dehydration to give diethyl ether (D = C₂H₅OC₂H₅, formula C₄H₁₀O): 2C₂H₅OH → C₂H₅OC₂H₅ + H₂O. Diethyl ether with excess HI gives ethyl iodide (E = C₂H₅I): C₂H₅OC₂H₅ + 2HI → 2C₂H₅I + H₂O.

(ii) प्रोपीन से प्रोपेन–1–ऑल

sub_questions.text_english:
Write the reagents which are used in the given conversions :
(i) Phenol to 2, 4, 6-tribromophenol
(ii) Propene to propan-1-ol
(iii) Butan-2-one to butan-2-ol

key_points: (i) Bromine water (Br₂/H₂O)
(ii) (a) B₂H₆ (diborane), then H₂O₂/NaOH (hydroboration-oxidation) OR (b) H₂SO₄ (anti-Markovnikov, via hydration with peroxide)
(iii) NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄ (reduction)

sub_questions.solution: (i) Phenol reacts with bromine water (Br₂/H₂O) to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol directly, since the –OH group strongly activates the ortho and para positions. (ii) Propene is converted to propan-1-ol (anti-Markovnikov addition) using hydroboration-oxidation: first diborane (B₂H₆) adds across the double bond (boron goes to less substituted carbon), then H₂O₂/NaOH oxidizes to give propan-1-ol. (iii) Butan-2-one is reduced to butan-2-ol using a reducing agent such as NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄, which reduces the ketone carbonyl group to a secondary alcohol.

sub_questions.text: एल्कीन के अम्ल उत्प्रेरित जलयोजन द्वारा संगत ऐल्कोहॉल बनने की क्रियाविधि को समझाइए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the mechanism of acid catalyzed hydration of alkene to form corresponding alcohol.

key_points: Step 1: Protonation of alkene by H⁺ (from H₃O⁺) to form carbocation (Markovnikov's rule — proton adds to less substituted carbon)
Step 2: Nucleophilic attack of water on the carbocation
Step 3: Loss of proton (deprotonation) to give alcohol

sub_questions.solution: The acid-catalyzed hydration of an alkene to give an alcohol proceeds via three steps. In the first step, the alkene acts as a Lewis base and accepts a proton (H⁺) from the acid (H₃O⁺), forming a carbocation intermediate. According to Markovnikov's rule, the proton adds to the carbon of the double bond that already bears more hydrogen atoms, producing the more stable (more substituted) carbocation. In the second step, a water molecule acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbocation, forming an oxonium ion (protonated alcohol). In the third step, the oxonium ion loses a proton to water, yielding the alcohol as the final product. For example, propene gives propan-2-ol (Markovnikov product) upon acid-catalyzed hydration.

आप निम्नलिखित का रूपान्तरण कैसे सम्पन्न करेंगे ?

sub_questions.text_english:
How will you convert the following :
(i) Propanone to Propene
(ii) Benzoic acid to Benzaldehyde
(iii) Benzene to m-Nitroacetophenone

key_points: (i) Propanone → (NaBH₄ or Grignard with CH₃MgX) → propan-2-ol → (conc. H₂SO₄/heat) → propene
(ii) Benzoic acid → (SOCl₂) → benzoyl chloride → (H₂/Pd-BaSO₄, Rosenmund) → benzaldehyde
(iii) Benzene → (CH₃COCl/AlCl₃, Friedel-Crafts acylation) → acetophenone → (HNO₃/H₂SO₄, nitration, meta director since acetyl group is deactivating) → m-nitroacetophenone

sub_questions.solution: (i) Propanone to Propene: Reduce propanone with NaBH₄ to get propan-2-ol. Then dehydrate propan-2-ol with concentrated H₂SO₄ at 443 K to get propene (CH₃CH=CH₂). (ii) Benzoic acid to Benzaldehyde: React benzoic acid with SOCl₂ to get benzoyl chloride (C₆H₅COCl). Then perform Rosenmund's reduction using H₂ over Pd/BaSO₄ (poisoned catalyst) to get benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO). (iii) Benzene to m-Nitroacetophenone: First, perform Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with CH₃COCl in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ to get acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃). Then, nitrate acetophenone with a mixture of concentrated HNO₃ and H₂SO₄. Since the –COCH₃ group is an electron-withdrawing (meta-directing) group, nitration occurs predominantly at the meta position to give m-nitroacetophenone.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को उनकी HCN के प्रति अभिक्रियाशीलता के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए : (CH₃)₂C=O, (CH₃)₃C·CO·C(CH₃)₃, CH₃CHO
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN : (CH₃)₂C=O, (CH₃)₃C·CO·C(CH₃)₃, CH₃CHO

key_points: (CH₃)₃C·CO·C(CH₃)₃ < (CH₃)₂C=O < CH₃CHO (increasing reactivity towards HCN)

sub_questions.solution: Reactivity towards HCN (nucleophilic addition) depends on the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon and steric hindrance. Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones because they have less steric crowding and less electron donation to the carbonyl carbon. Among ketones, greater steric bulk around the carbonyl reduces reactivity. Therefore the increasing order of reactivity towards HCN is: di-tert-butyl ketone (CH₃)₃C·CO·C(CH₃)₃ (most hindered, least reactive) < acetone (CH₃)₂C=O < acetaldehyde CH₃CHO (least hindered, most reactive).

sub_questions.text: उन यौगिकों की पहचान कीजिए जो ऐल्डॉल संघनन देंगे : HCHO, C₆H₅CHO, CH₃CHO, चक्रीय कीटोन
sub_questions.text_english: Identify the compounds which would undergo Aldol condensation : HCHO, C₆H₅CHO, CH₃CHO, cyclopentanone

key_points: CH₃CHO (acetaldehyde) and cyclopentanone undergo aldol condensation because they have α-hydrogen atoms. HCHO (formaldehyde) has no α-hydrogen. C₆H₅CHO (benzaldehyde) also has no α-hydrogen.

sub_questions.solution: Aldol condensation requires the presence of at least one α-hydrogen (hydrogen on the carbon adjacent to the carbonyl group). Acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO) has three α-hydrogens and readily undergoes aldol condensation. Cyclopentanone (the cyclic ketone shown) has α-hydrogens on both sides of the carbonyl and also undergoes aldol condensation. Formaldehyde (HCHO) has no α-carbon and cannot undergo self-aldol condensation. Benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO) also has no α-hydrogen and cannot undergo self-aldol condensation. Therefore, CH₃CHO and cyclopentanone undergo aldol condensation.

sub_questions.text_english:
Give chemical tests to distinguish between the following pairs of compounds :
(i) Acetophenone and Benzophenone
(ii) Propanal and Propanone
(iii) Pentan–2–one and Pentan–3–one

key_points: (i) Iodoform test: Acetophenone (CH₃COC₆H₅) has a CH₃CO– group and gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI₃) with I₂/NaOH. Benzophenone (C₆H₅COC₆H₅) does not have a CH₃CO– group and gives no iodoform.
(ii) Tollens' test or Fehling's test: Propanal (aldehyde) gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent or a red precipitate with Fehling's solution. Propanone (ketone) does not react.
(iii) Iodoform test: Pentan-2-one (CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃) has a CH₃CO– group and gives iodoform. Pentan-3-one (CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃) does not have CH₃CO– group and does not give iodoform.

sub_questions.solution: (i) Iodoform test: Treat each with I₂ and NaOH. Acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃) has a methyl ketone group (CH₃CO–) and gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI₃). Benzophenone (C₆H₅COC₆H₅) gives no iodoform. (ii) Tollens' test: Treat each with silver nitrate in ammoniacal solution (Tollens' reagent). Propanal (CH₃CH₂CHO), being an aldehyde, reduces Tollens' reagent to give a bright silver mirror on the test tube. Propanone (CH₃COCH₃), being a ketone, does not reduce Tollens' reagent and gives no silver mirror. (iii) Iodoform test: Treat each with I₂/NaOH. Pentan-2-one (CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃) contains the CH₃CO– group and gives a yellow iodoform precipitate. Pentan-3-one (CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃) does not contain CH₃CO– and gives no iodoform.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित अम्लों में से कौन प्रबलतर है और क्यों ? CH₂FCOOH, CH₃COOH
sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following acids is stronger and why ? CH₂FCOOH, CH₃COOH

key_points: CH₂FCOOH (fluoroacetic acid) is stronger because fluorine is highly electronegative and withdraws electron density from the carboxylate group through the inductive effect, stabilizing the carboxylate anion and facilitating proton release.

sub_questions.solution: CH₂FCOOH (fluoroacetic acid) is the stronger acid. The highly electronegative fluorine atom exerts a strong electron-withdrawing inductive effect (−I effect), which delocalizes the negative charge on the carboxylate anion (CH₂FCOO⁻) more effectively. This greater stabilization of the conjugate base means fluoroacetic acid releases its proton more readily, making it a stronger acid than acetic acid (CH₃COOH), where the CH₃ group has a weak electron-donating (+I) effect that destabilizes the carboxylate anion.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को उनके क्वथनांकों के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए : CH₃OCH₃, CH₃CH₂CH₃, CH₃CH₂OH, CH₃CHO
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their boiling points : CH₃OCH₃, CH₃CH₂CH₃, CH₃CH₂OH, CH₃CHO

key_points: CH₃CH₂CH₃ < CH₃OCH₃ < CH₃CHO < CH₃CH₂OH (increasing boiling point order)

sub_questions.solution: The increasing order of boiling points is: CH₃CH₂CH₃ (propane, −42°C) < CH₃OCH₃ (dimethyl ether, −24°C) < CH₃CHO (acetaldehyde, 20°C) < CH₃CH₂OH (ethanol, 78°C). Propane has only weak van der Waals forces, giving the lowest boiling point. Dimethyl ether has dipole-dipole interactions but no O–H groups for hydrogen bonding between ether molecules. Acetaldehyde has stronger dipole-dipole interactions (polar C=O). Ethanol has both intermolecular hydrogen bonding (O–H...O) and is the highest boiling of these four despite similar molecular mass to acetaldehyde, because H-bonds are much stronger than dipole-dipole forces.
